updates.name: [SUPERSEDED by QA-2684] Device-type choice offers only the three kinds of device that can be registered
updates.custom_requirements:
## Retired 2026-09-11 - do not automate

This case is a duplicate. The device-type list is already checked by **QA-2684 "Show only valid device types when registering a customer's phone"** (Done), which covers the same screen and the same rule: the legitimate choices are present and nothing else is.

The tablet option is not a separate case - it appears in that same list, on that same screen. Automating this case would run QA-2684 a second time under a different name.

Jira ticket QA-2825 was cancelled on 2026-09-11. Condition C-03 in the BYOT condition set is marked covered by QA-2684, not dropped.

If a future build changes what the device-type screen offers, update QA-2684 rather than reviving this case.

steps.action: Do not run this case - it is retired.
steps.expected: Run QA-2684 instead: Show only valid device types when registering a customer's phone.

updates.name: [SUPERSEDED by QA-2684 / QA-2686] Rep is stopped from moving on without naming the device kind
updates.custom_requirements:
## Retired 2026-09-11 - do not automate

This case is a duplicate. The rule that the rep cannot move past the device-type screen without making a choice is already covered by **QA-2684 "Show only valid device types when registering a customer's phone"** and **QA-2686 "Keep the chosen device type on the line through to carrier activation"** (both Done).

Nothing about that guard behaves differently when the device is a tablet.

Jira ticket QA-2826 was cancelled on 2026-09-11. Condition C-15 in the BYOT condition set is marked covered by QA-2684 and QA-2686, not dropped.

The check that a tablet line records the customer's own tablet correctly is still run - it lives on case 3781 (QA-2824).

steps.action: Do not run this case - it is retired.
steps.expected: Run QA-2684 and QA-2686 instead; for the tablet-specific checks run case 3781 (QA-2824).
